Tests freeze time and cover the exact-cutoff boundary, --days=0, an invalid-input dataset, zero users and the schedule expression
Clean diff: Pest.php was uncommented properly and imports are ordered

v.rationale: Both implementations look almost the same: an attribute-based command, a #[Scope] with a grouped whereNull/orWhere, a nullable timestamp migration with a datetime cast, Schedule::command(...)->dailyAt('06:00') in routes/console.php, and passing Pest suites (12 tests for impl-2, 11 for impl-1). In my probes they behaved the same on edge cases: both reject an empty --days and both reject '+5' and '007', both accept a huge value, and both group the OR correctly. The deciding difference is the requirement to run the command 'so the number shows up in our logs'. Inspecting the scheduled event shows impl-2's output goes to /dev/null, so the daily count disappears. impl-1 appends to storage/logs/inactive-users.log. impl-2 has the better code and tests: a pure cutoff-based scope, a factory state, frozen time, a boundary test and a tidier diff. impl-1 has small flaws: a leftover duplicate comment in Pest.php, unordered imports, '1 users' grammar, a heavier Validator and weaker tests. But a real requirement miss outweighs those, so impl-1 ranks first.
